classification.caveats: Segmentation upwind ends are offshore and approximate; wind varies locally and with height. FIRMS counts are rendered marker pixels, not individual detections. Summit thermal glow (45 px at Kilauea) is excluded and not used as eruption proof. Plume 1 upwind is ~70-85 km from summits and >85 km from nearest listed fire pixels, so exact fire of origin cannot be isolated from this context alone.
evidence: Both volcanoes officially not erupting at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW 'is not erupting', Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN 'erupting: no' on 2023-08-08
Two diffuse gray translucent veils leeward to west-southwest over ocean, not bright white textured trade cumulus seen elsewhere in image
Strong easterly 10-m flow ~30 km/h from ~83 deg at Maui fire site and ~31 km/h from 41 deg nearby, consistent with west / west-northwest elongation of veils
Multiple large FIRMS fire clusters on 2023-08-08: n=201 near Kula Maui, n=206 and n=46 near Kailua-Kona/Kohala Hawaii Island, n=21 near Mauna Loa flank, n=44 near Honolulu
Upwind ends are 69-85 km (plume 1) and 163-190 km (plume 2) from volcanic summits, not trailing from summit vents as expected for vog
Large broad light-gray diffuse veil west-southwest of Hawaii Island, not bright white cloud
Volcanoes not erupting per HVO, so not vog despite 68.9 km to Mauna Loa summit and 85.3 km to Kilauea summit from upwind end at 18.93N, -155.92W off SW coast
Coincident Hawaii Island wildfire activity: clusters n=206, n=46 near west Hawaii and n=21 Mauna Loa flank 17.2 km from summit (wildfire since no eruption)
Leeward position west of island under easterly trade flow favors smoke accumulation offshore
